used.how: Sized the win (an op's own output allocation ~35 us on 8x4) and chose caller-buffer options on the four forks, buffers from tt/host_alloc (P.15 pattern).
The forks are C++ ops already dispatching from the program cache, so the remaining host cost was output allocation, not program build.
The forks return a new Python wrapper of the given buffer; call sites keep the load-time object and never deallocate the returned wrapper.

missing: The fork test suites of rms_norm_ttnn (tests/unit) and mhc_post / mhc_pre (tests/golden) import a tt_ops_code_gen `eval` package absent from this tree (now DS41-173).
Which fork outputs outlive their layer (ffn_hc's hc, ffn_residual's stats row, mHC streams): no entry lists the cross-layer lifetimes; worked out from tt/mhc.py and tt/residual.py.

overseer.evidence: No padding or duplicated work: the forks only take an optional output buffer of exactly the spec they would allocate.
No Python-built op added or touched: rms_norm, mhc_post, mhc_pre_xing and rotary_embedding_indexed are C++ device ops (program cache, address override on a hit).

Attempt 2 ran no fork regression or unit suite and no device run; it only wrote the fork CHANGELOG/README/INDEX entries, BREADCRUMBS, known_issues DS41-173 (eval imports) and DS41-174, and this report.
No fork suites on the 8x4 in attempt 2; attempt 1's partial regression results are recorded in BREADCRUMBS for F.1.
